column1: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 450°F (232°C), or 400°F (204°C) with convection.
Bring 2 quarts (2 L) of water to a boil. Add 2 tbsp kosher salt, the baking soda and the potatoes, return to a boil, then simmer about 10 minutes until a knife slides in with little resistance.
Meanwhile warm the fat with the rosemary, garlic and some black pepper in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, about 3 minutes until the garlic just starts to turn golden.
Strain the oil right away into a large bowl and set the garlic and rosemary solids aside.
Drain the potatoes and let them steam dry in the pot for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes to the infused oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss vigorously until a thick starchy paste coats the chunks.
Spread the potatoes out on a large rimmed baking sheet and roast undisturbed for 20 minutes.
Loosen with a thin metal spatula, flip, and keep roasting another 30–40 minutes, shaking and turning a few times, until deep brown and crisp.
Toss the hot potatoes with the reserved garlic and rosemary plus the parsley, adjust salt and pepper, and serve right away.
